statement: Let $n$ be the number of ordered quadruples $(x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4)$ of positive odd integers that satisfy $\sum_{i=1}^4 x_i = 98$. Find $\dfrac{n}{100}$.
hint1: Use a generating function per variable
hint2: Each $x_i$ contributes factor $x+x^3+x^5+\cdots = \dfrac{x}{1-x^2}$; you need the coefficient of $x^{98}$ in $\left(\dfrac{x}{1-x^2}\right)^4$.
hint3: Substitute $x_i = 2y_i-1$ with $y_i\ge1$ to turn the condition into $\sum y_i = 51$, then use stars and bars: $n=\binom{50}{3}$.

textbook.title: generatingfunctionology (Wilf) - Chapter 1: Generating functions for combinatorial problems
